observation_summary: The argument matchers (e.g., anyString(), anyInt()) were incorrectly matching any input, including nulls and objects of different types, because they were all aliased to a generic 'Any' matcher.
hypothesis: The implementation of the anyX() family of matchers used a universal 'Any' matcher instead of performing type-specific validation. Changing these to use an 'InstanceOf' matcher ensures that the matchers only accept instances of the expected type and reject nulls.
prediction: The code will replace the 'Any.ANY' matcher with 'new InstanceOf(Type.class)' in all anyX() methods, enforcing strict type checking.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows that every instance of 'Any.ANY' in the Matchers class was replaced with 'new InstanceOf(Class.class)', which directly implements the required type-checking logic.
reasoning_summary: The defect was in the computational logic of the matcher methods. They were using an overly broad 'Any' matcher, which is a procedural/algorithmic error in how the matching strategy was implemented. The fix involved replacing this strategy with a more specific 'InstanceOf' check, which is a classic correction of an algorithmic/method-level procedure.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not about changing a single value or initialization, but about replacing the entire matching strategy (the algorithm) used by the methods.
While the fix adds type checking, it does so by replacing the underlying matcher object/strategy, which is a change to the method's implementation logic rather than just adding a guard clause.
